title: Asia stocks choppy as elevated yields temper Wall Street-led gains
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
Investing.com-- Asian stocks were mixed in choppy trade on Tuesday, as a record Nasdaq close overnight offered some support, while elevated U.S. Treasury yields and oil prices limited risk appetite.
Some Asian equities followed a strong Wall Street session. The Nasdaq rose 1.1% to a record close on Monday, while the S&P 500 gained 0.7% and the Dow rose 0.2%.
U.S. stock index futures traded largely unchanged as of 03:43 GMT.
Asia stocks lack direction amid surging yields
Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.6%, while the broader TOPIX index edged up 0.4%.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng added 0.6%, with the Hang Seng TECH sub-index climbing nearly 1%.
South Korea’s KOSPI, however, turned 1% lower after opening higher. Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) and SK Hynix (KS:000660) fell between 1.5% and 3%.
China’s onshore financial markets remained shut for the National Day and Golden Week holidays and will resume trading on Thursday, Oct. 8.
The 10-year Japanese government bond yield rose to 3.122% on Tuesday, reaching its highest since 2022, tracking the overnight rise in U.S. Treasury yields and expectations for further Bank of Japan policy tightening.
The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.349% overnight, its highest since 2002, while the 30-year yield reached 5.703%.
Elevated Treasury yields weigh on equities by raising borrowing costs and making bonds more attractive relative to riskier assets, particularly in high-growth technology shares.
RBI decision due this week; Brent remains above $100
Elsewhere, Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.6%, while Singapore’s Straits Times Index edged down 0.2%.
Futures tied to India’s Nifty 50 ticked down 0.1%.
Investors were looking ahead to the Reserve Bank of India’s policy decision on Wednesday, with markets expecting a 25-basis-point rate hike.
Markets also awaited the minutes of the Fed’s September meeting, due on Wednesday, for clues on policymakers’ views about inflation and the timing of further rate increases.
Oil prices remained a key risk. Brent crude was around $100 a barrel after falling 1.9% on Monday as Middle East exports increased and the Group of Seven pledged to boost supplies. Investors remained alert to renewed disruptions from the U.S.-Iran conflict.

title: Oil prices steady as markets weigh Aramco price cuts, M.East supplies
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
Investing.com-- Oil prices traded marginally higher on Tuesday, remaining under pressure after major producer Saudi Aramco unexpectedly cut November crude prices for Asia.
But renewed military tensions limited overall declines in crude, especially as Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis engaged in more hostilities this week.
Brent oil futures rose 0.3% to $100.60 a barrel by 22:10 ET (02:10 GMT), while West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 0.2% to $89.58 a barrel.
Get more insights on crude markets and the M.East war with InvestingPro
Crude falls on Aramco price cuts, improving M.East supplies
Crude was spooked by Saudi Aramco slashing its oil prices for Asian sales in November to a six-year low, while raising them slightly for northwest Europe and the Mediterranean.
The company was seen offering deep discounts for oil loaded off Oman to offset record-high freight rates, Reuters reported last week.
The price cuts also came amid growing concerns that overheated crude will dent global demand in the long term, especially as the war in the Middle East showed few signs of easing.
Still, crude fell sharply on Monday amid some signs of improving Middle East exports, while the Group of Seven nations also promised to increase supplies by 100 million barrels, although it was unclear whether the new oil would fall under an ongoing emergency release.
In the Middle East, Gulf oil exports rose to pre-war levels for about half of September, shipping data showed on Monday. This was driven by Saudi loading from both the Red Sea and the Gulf.
Saudi-Houthi clashes limit crude downside
Saudi-backed Yemeni forces retook coastal areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from the Iran-backed Houthis this week, spurring some hopes for improving Red Sea supplies.
The Houthis had earlier secured key positions along the strait and had launched missile strikes against ships in the region.
The Houthis retaliated against Monday’s offensive by attacking a slew of Saudi targets, including an Aramco refinery in Riyadh.
Saudi-Houthi fighting has remained squarely in focus since a dormant civil war re-emerged as a spillover of the U.S.-Iran conflict earlier this year.
The U.S. and Iran also remained at odds over the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Gold holds near $4,140 as dollar, yields offset lower Fed hike expectations
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
Investing.com -- Gold prices were little changed on Tuesday after recovering from their biggest weekly decline since June, as a stronger U.S. dollar and elevated Treasury yields offset support from fading expectations for another Federal Reserve rate hike.
At 20:44 ET (00:44 GMT), XAU/USD fell 0.1% to $4,138.09 an ounce, while Gold Futures rose 0.2% to $4,165.15. XAG/USD fell 0.1% to $60.998, while XPT/USD declined 0.2% to $1,721.37. The U.S. Dollar Index was little changed at 102.17.
Stronger dollar, Treasury yields weigh on gold
Gold's recovery has come as investors assess growing fiscal pressure around the world and the implications for monetary policy.
In Europe, political uncertainty and fiscal concerns in France have supported demand for the dollar. Policy gridlock triggered a selloff in more vulnerable European government debt and pushed the euro to a 17 month low, lifting the greenback toward its strongest levels of the year.
A stronger dollar typically pressures gold by making the metal more expensive for buyers using other currencies.
French debt concerns have also added to the broader rise in global bond yields. Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin warned that France could become increasingly constrained by high interest costs if it fails to improve its public finances, as French bond yields continued to rise.
U.S. Treasuries also came under fresh pressure Monday, with longer dated yields reaching new multi decade highs as the bond market extended a months long decline. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding gold, which does not generate interest income.
A U.S. Institute for Supply Management report showed cost pressures in the services sector rose last month at their fastest pace in more than four years. Persistent price pressures have kept the possibility of further Fed tightening alive, despite a weaker labor market.
Interest rate swaps were showing an almost 23% probability of an October Fed hike, while markets continued to price a full quarter point increase by the December meeting.
Weaker jobs data lowers near term rate hike bets
Gold has fallen more than 6% in September as energy driven inflation concerns, expectations for higher U.S. rates and a stronger dollar weighed on the metal.
However, expectations for an immediate Fed increase have eased sharply since last week's weaker than expected U.S. payrolls report. Fed officials have also been pushing back against expectations of an imminent hike.
That shift has provided some support for gold, even as rising bond yields remain a constraint.
The minutes of the Fed's September meeting, when policymakers raised interest rates for the first time in three years, are due midweek and could provide further guidance on the policy outlook.
ANZ analysts said gold has recovered from last week's sharp decline as investors reassess rising fiscal pressures globally.
They also pointed to lower expectations for rate hikes following the weaker payrolls data, with markets now assigning roughly a 20% chance of an October hike, down from around 70% a week earlier.

title: Trump signs order allowing road use of tax-exempt dyed diesel
full_text:
Investing.com-- U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday signed an executive order opening up general access to a tax-exempt, red dyed diesel as oil supply disruptions sent American fuel prices soaring.
The order defers the payment of Federal excise tax imposed for the on-road use of dyed diesel fuel for the remainder of the year, a White House factsheet showed on Monday evening.
Dyed diesel– typically colored red– is a tax exempt fuel used mainly for farming, and is banned from use on American highways. The fuel is almost chemically identical to on-road diesel, with the coloring intended as a tax-enforcement marker.
Trump’s exemption comes as U.S. diesel prices surged to record highs due to supply disruptions stemming from the Middle East and interruptions in refining due to the Russia-Ukraine war.
Diesel hit a record high of $6.529 a barrel in late-September.

Investors also weighed a softer U.S. services-sector reading that lowered near-term Fed hike expectations but pointed to persistent price pressures.
The U.S. dollar index was around 102.11, little changed, after reaching 102.21 and hitting an 18-month high in the previous session. The EUR/USD pair was around 1.123, while the GBP/USD pair rose marginally to 1.3224.

Dollar supported by yields, sticky inflation risks
The dollar's rally has continued despite weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs data that reduced expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike this month.
Investors are still betting that the Fed may need to tighten policy later as inflation risks remain elevated.
U.S. services-sector activity slowed in September, but stronger domestic demand put pressure on supply chains and pushed up prices paid by businesses for inputs.
The data suggested inflation could remain elevated into next year, limiting the scope for the Fed to ease policy aggressively.
The rise in Treasury yields has remained a key support for the dollar, with longer-dated U.S. borrowing costs still elevated as markets assess inflation, fiscal risks and the outlook for monetary policy.

title: Australian consumer sentiment falls more than expected as rate, fuel costs bite
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
Investing.com -- Australian consumer confidence deteriorated sharply, with households increasingly concerned about their finances, the economic outlook and jobs as cost-of-living pressures intensified, data from Westpac showed on Tuesday.
The Westpac-Melbourne Institute Consumer Sentiment Index fell 4.7% to 80.4 from 84.4 in September, missing a forecast 1.2% decline that would have put the index at about 83.4. The 80.4 reading was also among the weakest recorded since the survey began in the early 1970s.
Westpac said the latest Reserve Bank of Australia rate increase to 4.6%, the highest level since 2011, appears to have sharply rattled consumers.
Sentiment among the 60% of respondents surveyed before the rate decision was 86.9, but plunged to 67.2 among those surveyed after the announcement.
The nearly 20% difference between the pre- and post-RBA samples was the largest since Westpac began tracking daily survey responses in 2019, the bank said.
Fuel prices have also become a major drag, with average weekly pump prices rising above A$2.30 a litre, nearly 25% higher than at the start of the year. Meanwhile, the standard variable mortgage rate is expected to move above 9%, according to Westpac.
Westpac said pessimists outnumbered optimists in 102 of 106 consumer groups tracked by the survey, while more than 80% of consumers expected mortgage rates to rise over the next year.
The report also showed growing unease about the jobs outlook, suggesting pressure on household finances is broadening beyond inflation and borrowing costs.

title: Anthropic tells Australia it’s open to laws requiring reporting of AI agent hacks
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
By Byron Kaye
SYDNEY, Oct 6 (Reuters) - Anthropic does not believe its products have breached Australian government systems but would be open to Australian laws requiring AI companies to disclose data breaches, company executives told an Australian parliamentary inquiry on Tuesday.
Their statements come weeks after rival OpenAI disclosed one of its agents broke into the country’s main health portal and as the companies wait for approval for massive data centres planned in Sydney and regional Queensland.
Anthropic, creator of AI chatbot Claude, and ChatGPT maker OpenAI also want Australia to relax its copyright laws so they can use local content to train models.
Australia, which is readying AI-specific laws that will take effect next year, rebuked OpenAI in September after the US tech firm notified it of a breach of the Medicare portal some three months earlier.
Both firms are under scrutiny worldwide after incidents in which their AI agents have gone rogue to hack external systems, learning to bend rules, exploit loopholes and interact with external systems.
Anthropic Head of Safeguards David Orr told the parliamentary inquiry into AI that a "lengthy, deep investigation" since an OpenAI agent’s hack of Hugging Face, showed there had been no breaches of Australian government systems.
"We haven’t found anything like this, and we have looked," he said.
The company had "much less visibility on what has happened for our customers", Orr noted, since enterprise customers typically had stricter rules on data deletion.
Whether a company reported a breach of government data was most likely determined by the company’s internal policy, not the law, Orr said. Anthropic’s head of policy for Australia and New Zealand, David Masters, told the inquiry the company would be open to Australian laws requiring AI companies to disclose data breaches.
At the inquiry, Australian content creators pushed back against attempts by AI companies to relax copyright laws which currently require the mostly foreign-domiciled tech companies to negotiate licencing deals before using their material for model training.
"The copyright system is completely adequate to manage the business of AI," said Kate Gilchrist, the head of content and legal operations for national broadcaster the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.
Media reports have said the Australian government was considering an "opt out" clause for AI companies, effectively giving the AI companies access to content unless a rightsholder objects, but that "places the burden on rightsholders", said Gilchrist.
"We cannot scour the internet and ensure that we are opting out on all those sites. It simply does not work," she said.
The Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence is one of at least four Australian state and federal inquiries into the technology.
Representatives of OpenAI are scheduled to appear at the same inquiry later on Tuesday.

title: Exclusive-Accenture contractor removed from FBI following damaging data breach, sources say
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
By Jana Winter and Raphael Satter
WASHINGTON, Oct 5 (Reuters) - The Federal Bureau of Investigation removed an Accenture contractor on Monday over their role in a damaging data breach that exposed sensitive personal details of thousands of bureau employees, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.
The development comes as the FBI is still trying to ascertain the ramifications of the breach, which some former bureau officials have described as a major blow to the organization’s operational security.
In a statement to Reuters, a senior FBI official confirmed that an unidentified contractor had failed to properly update — or patch — the system they were responsible for.
"To date, our review has determined that the incident occurred as the result of a security failure of a platform managed by a third-party organization — after a contractor failed to implement a security patch explicitly issued to secure the platform," FBI cyber chief Brett Leatherman said in the statement. "As such, the FBI has removed the contractor and taken all necessary steps to both mitigate any further risk and protect our workforce."
The FBI did not identify the platform or third-party organization, but the two sources familiar with the matter said the platform was Oracle’s PeopleSoft, a human resources platform that the hacking group ShinyHunters said it exploited to break into the FBI’s job site last month.
Oracle did not immediately reply to a request for comment.
The sources also said the third-party organization was Accenture. Reuters could not immediately identify the specific contractor or determine their current employment status.
In a statement, Accenture said it was "proud to support the mission of the FBI and will continue to do so." It did not answer questions about the contractor or their alleged failure to patch.
CRITICAL PATCHES
In June, Google raised the alarm over a ShinyHunters-linked hack-and-extort campaign aimed at organizations using PeopleSoft software. The same day, Oracle issued a security alert identifying a weakness in PeopleSoft and offering security fixes.
Both companies urged organizations running PeopleSoft to "apply all Critical Patch Updates, Critical Security Patch Updates and Security Alerts without delay."
Swift patching of vulnerable software is considered a key part of defending networks and devices against hackers, but the process can be laborious and difficult, particularly with enterprise software that serves large numbers of people.
Reuters has not been able to determine whether or when those responsible for securing the FBI’s job site followed those recommendations, but ShinyHunters credited a vulnerability in PeopleSoft for facilitating its intrusion.
The breach has triggered concern across the FBI and the wider intelligence community, exposing sensitive personal information, including granular descriptions of named employees’ counterintelligence jobs, street addresses of human intelligence operatives, and medical and psychiatric records of bureau workers.
Last week, a key ShinyHunters suspect was detained in Jordan, Reuters reported. Sources told Reuters the alleged hacker was cooperating, a development that may help the bureau limit — or at the very least understand — the scope of the damage.

A decline in oil prices helped to marginally soothe some concerns around persistent energy-driven inflation, although expectations that the Federal Reserve will skip an interest rate hike this month before raising borrowing costs in December were little changed.
Meanwhile, a fresh set of services sector activity data showed that the prices paid by these companies in September touched a post-2022 high, keeping inflation worries in play. With the Fed tipped to remain focused on corralling price gains, the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in more than two decades, limiting the climb in stocks in the process.
Investors were also assessing fears that the U.S. bond-market woes may be spreading globally, particularly in France. However, analysts at Deutsche Bank said that there were "initial signs that the pressure on France was stabilizing, with a clear outperformance in French debt."
2. Gulf oil exports topped pre-war levels for half of September, data shows
Gulf oil exporters managed to surpass pre-war levels for roughly half of September, according to shipping data cited by Reuters.
Kpler data showed the seven-day moving average for crude exports from the region stood at 18.3 million barrels per day on September 30, with volumes exceeding levels before the start of the Iran war in late February for 14 days last month.
The figures appeared to bolster hopes that crude flows have been managing to make their way out of the Gulf, despite the near-constant threat of attacks on tankers and other commercial vessels.
Iran moved to all but shutter the Strait of Hormuz following the outbreak of the war, cutting off a vital waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before the fighting began. The conflict has since expanded into other parts of the Gulf, including to Yemen, where Iran-backed Houthi militants and Saudi-aligned government forces are grappling for control over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, another critical shipping conduit.
Analysts at Vital Knowledge suggested that while the volume of oil exiting the Middle East is "fairly healthy considering all the turmoil," the cost of taking a barrel of crude through Hormuz is "substantially higher than before the war." As a result, prices paid by end customers will stay elevated for the foreseeable future, they added.
Benchmark Brent crude futures were last trading lower by 0.8% at $99.53 a barrel.
3. Constellation Brands earnings ahead
On a relatively quiet earnings calendar, Constellation Brands is slated to report after the closing bell.
Constellation, whose brands include beers like Corona and Modelo Especial lager, is tipped to post comparable operating profit of $872.3 million on comparable net sales of $2.53 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.
In June, the company notched better-than-estimated fiscal first-quarter profit and reiterated its fiscal 2027 adjusted profit per share outlook of $11.20 to $11.90. Analysts said that the FIFA World Cup soccer tournament and a moderation in oil prices at the time helped to boost demand.
Although the wider alcohol market in the U.S. remains under pressure, partly because of continued uncertainty around inflation, brewers have been moving to slash their prices and focus their marketing campaigns to prop up sales.
4. U.S. trade balance figures
Elsewhere, a new batch of U.S. trade figures for August will be unveiled on Tuesday.
In July, the U.S. trade deficit widened due to solid import demand, putting trade in a position to weigh down on wider economic growth in the third quarter. Data from the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau showed that the trade shortfall rose by 24.4% to $88.6 billion in July.
Imports, in particular, increased 2.8% to $399.3 billion. Domestic demand has been boosted in recent months by resilient customer spending, as well as a boom in expenditures on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

title: German yields drop as markets seek shelter, leaving French OATs sidelined
full_text:
Investing.com -- Eurozone government bond bourses continued to fragment on Tuesday, as global fixed-income allocators poured capital into safe-haven German paper while keeping French sovereign debt on a tight leash amid deep-seated fiscal anxieties.
French benchmark yields were largely flat on the day, with the 10-year OAT yield consolidating near multi-decade highs of 4.776%.
In stark contrast, Germany’s 10-year government bond yield - the primary risk-free benchmark for the single-currency bloc - extended its downward trajectory, dropping further TO 3.432%.
Flight to quality anchors German bunds
The ongoing flight to quality highlights a growing reluctance among institutional desks to absorb French debt, even after the violent yield spike seen earlier in the week.
German yields extended their decline across the curve, reflecting steady demand for liquid, high-grade European paper as market participants seek shelter from continental political and fiscal friction.
The yield spread between 10-year French OATs and German Bunds remained close to 140 bps, entrenched near 2012 peaks, as international buyers continue to demand a steep risk premium to hold French paper relative to German risk-free benchmarks.
Fiscal woes and 2027 election gridlock weigh on Paris
Behind the persistent cold shoulder toward French duration paper are deep structural concerns over the nation’s public finances and political stability.
With France’s budget deficit projected at 5.4% of GDP this year and public debt hovering near a record 120% of GDP, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu’s proposed €54 billion fiscal consolidation package faces a daunting legislative path.
Fears of protracted political gridlock in Parliament - coupled with early maneuvering ahead of the 2027 presidential election - have left fixed-income desks skeptical that Paris can enforce spending cuts without sparking broader domestic unrest or political paralysis.
As a result, global bondholders continue to steer clear of French paper, favoring German Bunds as the primary haven within the single-currency bloc.
Japanese bonds pare losses
Tokyo’s 10-year yield, was up to 3.1%. According to Reuters, demand at a sale of the securities rose to its highest since May.
Meanwhile, the Japanese 30-year note yield, which hit a record high of 4.24% on Monday, was little changed at 4.235%.

title: Genmab jumps as its lymphoma drug combo with AbbVie cuts progression, death risk
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
Investing.com -- Shares of Genmab surged more than 8% in early trading Tuesday after the Danish biotech and AbbVie said their combination treatment for newly diagnosed patients with a type of lymphoma reduced the risk of disease progression or death in a late-stage study.
The Phase 3 trial tested epcoritamab alongside R-CHOP, the current standard of care, in patients newly diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, the most common form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The combination cut the risk of progression or death by 51% compared with R-CHOP alone, the companies said.
They said it is the first late-stage study of a bispecific antibody combination to significantly improve progression-free survival, meaning how long patients live without their cancer worsening, in first-line DLBCL. The safety profile was generally consistent with the known profiles of epcoritamab and R-CHOP.
Epcoritamab, which Genmab and AbbVie are developing jointly, is an immune-based therapy that helps the body’s T cells attack cancer cells. It has not yet been approved for patients who have just been diagnosed and have not received prior treatment.
"DLBCL is an aggressive disease and the need to advance treatment options is critical. These positive topline results suggest that epcoritamab combined with R-CHOP could offer a potential new standard of care in newly diagnosed DLBCL patients," said Daejin Abidoye, vice president and oncology head at AbbVie.
"These topline results of epcoritamab in combination with R-CHOP mark the first Phase 3 study to demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival in patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL treated with a bispecific antibody combination and have the potential to reshape the frontline treatment landscape," said Jan van de Winkel, CEO of Genmab.
Separately, Barclays analysts saw the result as a strong validation of epcoritamab in frontline DLBCL, which represents the drug’s largest commercial opportunity.

Investing.com -- Informa on Tuesday announced plans to buy events organizer Clarion from Blackstone for an enterprise value of £2.24 billion, or about $3 billion, and said it will separate its Taylor & Francis academic publishing arm to focus on business-to-business events.
The deal values Clarion at 11.1 times expected 2027 EBITDA, falling to about 9 times when £50 million of annual run-rate cost savings are included. Informa expects it to lift adjusted diluted earnings per share by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2027, with a post-tax return on invested capital above 10% by 2029.
Clarion owns more than 100 B2B event brands, including Germany’s IFA consumer electronics show, the DSEI defense exhibition and the ICE gaming event in Barcelona. It is expected to generate revenue of more than £575 million in 2027, with adjusted operating margins above 30%.
Informa said the combination would create the leading U.K.-listed B2B events operator, with group revenue above $6 billion and underlying growth of around 7%. It also identified £25 million in additional operating profit from revenue synergies by 2029.
Informa will fund the purchase with acquisition financing and a roughly £940 million equity raise, equal to about 9% of its share capital, consisting of an institutional placing and a retail offer. It will pause its share buyback. The company expects net debt to EBITDA to stay below 3 times at year-end and fall below 2.5 times by the end of 2027. Completion is expected late in the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approvals.
Taylor & Francis, which has revenue approaching $1 billion and is growing about 4% a year, will go through a formal separation review. The outcome will be reported with full-year results in March 2027. Informa did not say whether it favors a sale or a spin-off.
"With Taylor & Francis approaching $1bn in revenue, growing at 4%± and with its Open Research capabilities firmly established, we believe it will now benefit from greater flexibility and freedom through the next phase of its development, as Informa further expands the depth and reach of its B2B portfolio," said Chief Executive Stephen Carter.
Blackstone bought Clarion in 2017 from Providence Equity Partners for £600 million.

Conversely, production and supply-chain issues, programme delays, adverse product mix and weaker working-capital conversion could weigh on the shares.

title: BOJ chief calls for more focus on anchoring inflation around target
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
By Leika Kihara
TOKYO, Oct 6 (Reuters) - Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Tuesday it was becoming more important to anchor underlying inflation around the central bank’s 2% target, signalling readiness to keep raising interest rates to blunt the risk of too-high inflation.
The remarks come ahead of the central bank’s two-day policy meeting ending on October 30, where new quarterly growth and inflation forecasts will be closely watched for clues on the timing of the next rate hike.
Ueda said economic and price developments were broadly in line with the BOJ’s forecasts, with the economy recovering moderately and the central bank’s "tankan" survey pointing to solid business sentiment.
Rising raw material costs are pushing up wholesale inflation with price pressures spreading to consumer inflation, Ueda said, adding that long-term inflation expectations continue to rise.
He also warned of the risk of underlying inflation overshooting the BOJ’s target due to price pressures from the US-Israeli war on Iran, strong AI-related demand and the weak yen.
"Financial conditions remain accommodative and continue to underpin economic activity" even after last month’s rate hike, Ueda said, adding that the central bank will continue to raise borrowing costs to adjust the level of monetary support.
"It has become more important than before to ensure underlying inflation becomes anchored around 2%" so that the risk of an inflation overshoot does not materialise and damage the economy, he added.
In a statement announcing the September rate hike, the BOJ said only that it was "important" to anchor underlying inflation around the BOJ’s target.
The BOJ raised its key rate to a 31-year high last month, with Ueda signalling the central bank had entered a phase focused on preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its target, raising the prospect of tighter policy.

title: European shares gain as Genmab jumps, bond yields retreat
full_text:
Wall Street ends within sight of record close as traders brush off bond rout
Oct 6 (Reuters) - European shares rose to near one-week highs on Tuesday, as Genmab led gains in healthcare stocks, while euro zone bond yields took a breather after rallying on fiscal and inflation concerns.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index was up 0.8% to 638.41 points by 0727 GMT, poised for a third straight session of gains.
Genmab climbed 7.6% to the top of STOXX 600 after the Danish biotech firm and US drugmaker AbbVie’s blood cancer drug combination cut risk of progression or death in a late-stage study.
The broader healthcare sector was up 1.6%.
Attention now turns to euro zone retail sales data and the UK S&P Global PMI survey due later in the day, which could offer clues about the region’s consumer spending and Britain’s economic activity.
The euro hovered near a 17-month low, weighed down by political uncertainty after Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap election on Monday.
Meanwhile, the French government is seeking to enact an unpopular 2027 budget to lower its deficit, sparking a rout in bonds.
Still, euro zone bond yields eased, having touched multi-decade highs last week. [GVD/EUR]
Among other stocks, Italy’s Technoprobe gained 2.3% after J.P.Morgan initiated coverage on the stock with an "overweight" rating.
